headline: Federal Reserve Signals Slower Rate Cuts Amid Persistent Inflation Pressures
summary: The Federal Reserve indicated it may slow the pace of interest rate cuts after November CPI data showed inflation remaining above the 2% target. Fed Chair Powell reiterated that monetary policy will remain data-dependent, with FOMC members projecting fewer rate cuts in 2026 than previously anticipated. Markets repriced rate expectations sharply, with the 10-year Treasury yield rising 15 basis points.

headline: NVIDIA Posts Record Q3 Revenue on AI Chip Demand, Raises Guidance
summary: NVIDIA reported record quarterly revenue of $35.1 billion, up 94% year-over-year, driven by insatiable demand for its H100 and Blackwell GPU chips used in AI and machine learning workloads. The semiconductor giant raised full-year guidance and announced a new $50 billion share buyback program. Data centre revenue reached $30.8 billion, with hyperscalers AWS, Azure, and GCP among the largest buyers.

headline: Bitcoin Surpasses $100,000 Milestone as Institutional Demand Accelerates
summary: Bitcoin crossed the $100,000 level for the first time, driven by record inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs and growing institutional adoption. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust recorded its highest single-day inflow of $1.2 billion. Analysts cited a favourable regulatory environment and the post-halving supply squeeze as key drivers. Ethereum also surged, trading above $3,800.

headline: Brent Crude Drops Below $70 as OPEC+ Delays Production Cut Extension
summary: Brent crude oil prices fell sharply after OPEC+ members failed to reach consensus on extending production cuts beyond Q1 2026. Saudi Arabia and Russia signalled willingness to gradually unwind cuts, while non-OPEC supply from the US and Brazil continues to rise. EIA data showed US crude inventories rising by 4.2 million barrels last week, adding further downward pressure on WTI and brent crude prices.

headline: JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs Beat Q4 Estimates as Investment Banking Recovers
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs both reported fourth-quarter earnings that exceeded analyst expectations, boosted by a rebound in investment banking fees and strong trading revenues. JPM reported net interest margin of 2.7% while Goldman's equities trading desk posted its best quarter in three years. Bank earnings across the sector benefited from higher-for-longer rates and robust M&A activity.

headline: China GDP Growth Slows to 4.6% in Q3, Missing Official Target
summary: China's economy grew 4.6% year-on-year in the third quarter, falling short of Beijing's 5% full-year target amid continued weakness in the property sector and sluggish consumer demand. The China property sector remains under severe stress, with new home sales declining 25% year-on-year. Evergrande's liquidation proceedings continue to weigh on market sentiment. The People's Bank of China cut reserve requirement ratios to stimulate loan growth.

headline: EUR/USD Falls to 1.04 as ECB Signals Aggressive Rate Cut Path
summary: The EUR/USD exchange rate fell to a two-year low of 1.04 after ECB President Lagarde signalled the central bank could cut rates faster than previously projected if eurozone economic weakness persists. German industrial output fell 4.1% in October, adding to recessionary fears. Dollar strength, underpinned by the DXY index rising above 106, continued to pressure the euro and other major currencies in foreign exchange markets.

headline: Microsoft Azure AI Revenue Surges 33% as Enterprise Adoption Accelerates
summary: Microsoft reported Azure cloud revenue growth of 33% in its fiscal Q2, with AI services contributing 12 percentage points of that growth. The company's AI & machine learning tools, including Copilot integrations across Office 365 and Azure OpenAI Service, drove record enterprise contract signings. CEO Satya Nadella highlighted that AI is now the fastest-growing product in Microsoft's history, with MSFT shares rising 4% after hours.

headline: US-China Trade War Escalates with New Semiconductor Export Controls
summary: The Biden administration announced sweeping new export controls targeting advanced semiconductor chips and chip-making equipment destined for China, escalating US-China trade tensions. The restrictions cover chips used in AI and machine learning applications, including those from NVIDIA and AMD. Beijing responded with counter-sanctions on rare earth elements critical to US defence and technology industries, raising fears of further deglobalisation.

headline: Gold Hits All-Time High of $2,800 as Safe Haven Demand Surges
summary: Gold prices surged to an all-time high of $2,800 per troy ounce, driven by geopolitical risk from the Middle East conflict, central bank buying, and expectations of further Fed rate cuts in 2026. The XAU/USD pair broke decisively above key resistance levels as real yields fell. Central banks purchased a record 1,037 tonnes of gold in 2025, with China, Poland, and India the largest buyers, according to the World Gold Council.

headline: Apple Intelligence AI Features Drive iPhone 16 Supercycle Expectations
summary: Analysts upgraded Apple to buy citing AI-driven upgrade cycle expectations, as iPhone 16 sales data from Asia supply chains showed record pre-orders. Apple's on-device AI and machine learning features, marketed as Apple Intelligence, are seen as the primary catalyst for the first major iPhone upgrade supercycle since 2021. AAPL shares hit a record high, pushing the company's market cap above $3.8 trillion.

headline: US CPI Rises 2.7% in November, Core Inflation Remains Sticky
summary: US Consumer Price Index rose 2.7% year-on-year in November, slightly above the 2.6% consensus estimate, with core CPI excluding food and energy holding at 3.3%. Services inflation remains the primary driver, particularly shelter costs which rose 4.7%. The data complicates the Fed's monetary policy path and reinforced market expectations that the FOMC will pause rate cuts early in 2026.

headline: Russia-Ukraine Ceasefire Talks Stall as Winter Offensive Intensifies
summary: Diplomatic efforts to broker a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire collapsed after Moscow rejected a US-brokered peace framework, escalating the conflict ahead of winter. Ukraine's energy infrastructure suffered new attacks, raising concerns about European energy security. Natural gas prices in Europe spiked 15% on fears of supply disruptions via remaining pipeline routes. NATO allies pledged additional military aid at an emergency Brussels summit.

headline: Private Equity Dry Powder Hits Record $2.5 Trillion as Deal Activity Stalls
summary: Global private equity dry powder reached a record $2.5 trillion as elevated interest rates and tight credit conditions continue to suppress leveraged buyout activity. PE exits and IPO pipeline activity remain well below historical norms, with the secondaries market seeing elevated volumes as LPs seek liquidity. Family offices and endowment allocations to private markets are expected to increase as fund managers offer more flexible structures.

headline: EU Carbon Border Tax CBAM Enters Full Implementation Phase
summary: The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered its full implementation phase, requiring importers of steel, cement, aluminium, fertilisers, and electricity to pay for embedded carbon emissions. The carbon border tax is a landmark ESG regulation designed to prevent carbon leakage and incentivise global emissions reductions. European steel and aluminium producers welcomed the measure while trading partners including China and India filed formal WTO objections.

headline: Ethereum ETF Inflows Surpass Bitcoin ETF in First Week of Launch
summary: Newly launched spot Ethereum ETFs attracted $1.8 billion in their first week of trading, surpassing Bitcoin ETF inflows at the equivalent stage of their launch. Institutional demand for Ethereum was driven by staking yield expectations and growing adoption of the DeFi ecosystem. The crypto regulation environment improved markedly following SEC guidance clarifying the treatment of staking income from digital assets.

headline: US Mortgage Rates Fall to 6.4% as Fed Signals More Cuts Ahead
summary: US 30-year fixed mortgage rates fell to 6.4%, the lowest level in 18 months, after the Fed signalled continued easing of monetary policy. Housing starts rose 8.2% in November as lower mortgage rates drew buyers back into the residential housing market. The Case-Shiller home price index showed national home prices up 4.2% year-on-year, with the most significant gains in Sun Belt markets. REITs rallied on the rate outlook improvement.

headline: India Surpasses China as World's Fastest-Growing Major Economy
summary: India's GDP growth accelerated to 7.4% in the September quarter, cementing its position as the world's fastest-growing major economy ahead of China. India growth is being driven by record infrastructure spending under the Modi government's National Infrastructure Pipeline, strong domestic consumption, and booming services exports. Foreign direct investment into India reached a record $85 billion in 2025, with technology and manufacturing the top sectors.

headline: Clean Energy Investment Breaks $1 Trillion Barrier for First Time
summary: Global investment in clean energy and ESG-aligned infrastructure surpassed $1 trillion for the first time in 2025, according to BloombergNEF. Solar and wind energy accounted for 65% of new power capacity additions globally, while green bonds issuance reached $900 billion. Net zero commitments from major corporates accelerated, with over 3,000 companies now enrolled in Science Based Targets initiative. The EU ETS carbon price held above €60 per tonne.

headline: US National Debt Hits $36 Trillion as Budget Deficit Widens
summary: US national debt crossed $36 trillion for the first time, with the annual federal budget deficit projected to reach $1.9 trillion in fiscal year 2025. Moody's placed the US sovereign credit rating on negative watch, citing structural fiscal imbalances and rising interest payments that now consume 18% of federal revenue. Debate over tax policy and the upcoming debt ceiling deadline dominated congressional hearings this week.

headline: Fed Cuts Rates by 25bps, Projects Only Two Cuts in 2026
summary: The Federal Reserve cut its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 4.25%–4.5% at its December FOMC meeting, as expected. The updated dot plot showed median projections of only two rate cuts in 2026, down from four projected in September. Fed Chair Powell emphasised that inflation remains above target and that the pace of further easing will be gradual and data-dependent. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 10bps on the hawkish guidance.

headline: China Property Sector Rescue Package Fails to Arrest Home Price Decline
summary: Beijing's latest stimulus package for the China property sector, including cuts to down-payment requirements and mortgage rates, failed to stop the decline in new home prices which fell for the 17th consecutive month. Country Garden's restructuring talks with offshore creditors remain unresolved, while developer land purchases fell 35% year-on-year. The China property sector downturn is estimated to have wiped $18 trillion in household wealth since 2021.

headline: Venture Capital Funding Rebounds 40% in 2025 Driven by AI Startups
summary: Global venture capital funding rebounded 40% in 2025 to $380 billion, driven almost entirely by artificial intelligence and machine learning startups. OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI collectively raised over $20 billion. The VC ecosystem shifted sharply toward AI infrastructure, with investors backing startups building data centres, AI chips, and foundation model layers. Traditional sectors including fintech and e-commerce saw continued funding pressure amid higher cost of capital.

headline: Dollar Index DXY Climbs to 108, Strongest Level Since 2022
summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY) climbed to 108, its strongest level since 2022, driven by the Federal Reserve's hawkish guidance, robust US economic data, and capital flows into US assets. Dollar strength weighed heavily on emerging market currencies, with the EM FX basket falling 3% in December. The strong greenback also pressured commodity prices denominated in dollars, with gold and brent crude retreating from recent highs.

headline: OPEC+ Agrees to Delay Oil Output Increase Until Q2 2026
summary: OPEC+ members reached a compromise agreement to delay the planned unwinding of production cuts until April 2026, providing temporary support to crude oil prices. Brent crude recovered above $72 on the news. Saudi Arabia's Energy Minister cited global economic uncertainty and elevated non-OPEC supply as justification for maintaining current OPEC+ production discipline. EIA forecasts US oil production at a record 13.5 million barrels per day in 2026.

headline: S&P 500 Posts Best Annual Performance Since 1997, Rising 23%
summary: The S&P 500 ended 2025 with a gain of 23%, its best annual performance since 1997, driven by the AI investment boom, resilient corporate earnings, and Federal Reserve rate cuts. Tech stocks and semiconductors led returns, with NVDA rising 177%, MSFT 38%, and AAPL 29% for the year. The equal-weighted S&P 500 returned a more modest 13%, highlighting continued market concentration in mega-cap technology names.

headline: Middle East Tensions Spike as Houthi Attacks Disrupt Red Sea Shipping
summary: Houthi forces in Yemen intensified attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea, forcing major shipping companies to reroute vessels around the Cape of Good Hope. The disruption extended transit times by 10–14 days and pushed freight rates sharply higher. The Middle East conflict risk spread to oil markets, with Brent crude rising 4% on supply chain disruptions fears. US and UK naval forces conducted strikes on Houthi missile sites in response.

headline: Cybersecurity Spending to Hit $300 Billion in 2026 as AI Threats Evolve
summary: Global cybersecurity spending is forecast to reach $300 billion in 2026, up 15% from 2025, as organisations respond to a surge in AI-powered cyberattacks, ransomware, and data breaches. CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Palo Alto Networks (PANW) both raised full-year guidance. The cybersecurity sector attracted $15 billion in venture capital funding and is increasingly viewed as critical national infrastructure by G7 governments.

headline: ESG Fund Outflows Continue as Greenwashing Scrutiny Intensifies
summary: ESG-labelled funds recorded their fifth consecutive quarter of net outflows in Q4 2025, totalling $45 billion, as investors questioned the ESG ratings methodology and performance of sustainable products. The SEC's climate disclosure regulations require companies to report Scope 1 and 2 emissions from 2026, putting additional compliance pressure on asset managers. Several major banks revised their net zero commitments downward amid political and legal pressure.

headline: Bank of Japan Raises Rates for Second Time, Yen Surges Against Dollar
summary: The Bank of Japan raised interest rates by 25 basis points to 0.5%, its second hike in 2025, citing rising inflation and improving wage growth. The USD/JPY pair fell sharply from 157 to 151 as carry trades unwound, pressuring risk assets globally. Japanese government bond yields rose to their highest level since 2011. The BoJ's hawkish pivot is reshaping global capital flows as the yen becomes less attractive as a funding currency.

headline: Trump Administration Announces Sweeping Tariffs on Chinese Imports
summary: The incoming Trump administration announced plans to impose 60% tariffs on all Chinese goods and 10% universal tariffs on imports from other countries, escalating US-China trade tensions significantly. The measures, framed as reshoring and nearshoring policy tools, are expected to raise consumer prices and disrupt global supply chains. The Chinese yuan weakened to 7.35 per dollar, and US equity futures fell 1.5% on the announcement.

headline: US Non-Farm Payrolls Surge 256,000 in December, Beating Forecasts
summary: The US economy added 256,000 jobs in December, significantly beating the consensus estimate of 165,000 and signalling continued labour market resilience. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%. Wage growth moderated slightly to 3.9% year-on-year. The strong NFP report reduced expectations for Fed rate cuts, sending Treasury yields higher and the DXY index above 109. The robust labour market supports the soft-landing narrative but complicates inflation control.

headline: BlackRock Launches $30 Billion Private Credit Fund, Largest Ever
summary: BlackRock launched a $30 billion private credit direct lending fund, the largest ever raised by a single asset manager, signalling the mainstreaming of private markets. The fund targets leveraged buyout financing and corporate middle-market lending. Private credit has grown to a $1.7 trillion asset class globally as banks retreated from leveraged loan markets following Basel III/IV capital requirement increases. Family offices and sovereign wealth funds are the primary limited partners.

headline: Inflation Expectations Rise as Tariff Fears Grip Bond Markets
summary: US 10-year breakeven inflation expectations rose to 2.5%, the highest since 2023, as bond markets priced in the inflationary impact of proposed tariffs and fiscal stimulus. The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 4.8%, putting pressure on equity valuations. Fed officials pushed back against expectations for rate cuts, with Governor Waller stating policy will remain restrictive until inflation convincingly returns to 2%. The bond market's inflation expectations are now at odds with the Fed's projections.

headline: Taiwan Strait Tensions Rise as China Conducts Military Exercises
summary: China conducted its largest military exercises near Taiwan in two years, sending 90 aircraft and 11 warships into the Taiwan Strait and surrounding waters. The exercises, framed as a response to US arms sales to Taiwan, rattled semiconductor supply chain investors given Taiwan's dominant role in chip manufacturing. TSMC shares fell 5% in Taipei trading. The US deployed an additional carrier strike group to the region in response.

headline: Bitcoin Retreats 20% from Peak as Regulatory Fears Return
summary: Bitcoin fell 20% from its record high above $100,000, triggering $2 billion in leveraged crypto liquidations across exchanges. The sell-off was sparked by reports that the SEC is investigating several stablecoin issuers for potential violations of crypto regulation rules. Ethereum fell 18% and the broader digital asset market lost $400 billion in market capitalisation within 48 hours. Long-term holders absorbed much of the selling pressure.

headline: Meta AI Expansion Drives Q4 Revenue Beat, Zuckerberg Raises Capex Guidance
summary: Meta Platforms reported Q4 revenue of $48.4 billion, up 21% year-on-year, driven by AI-powered advertising optimisation and strong engagement across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced plans to spend $60–65 billion in 2026 on AI infrastructure including GPUs, data centres, and model development. The spending increase reflects Meta's strategy to embed artificial intelligence across all its consumer and enterprise products.

headline: ECB Cuts Rates for Fourth Time, Signals Pause Ahead
summary: The European Central Bank cut its key deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% at its January meeting, the fourth cut in the current easing cycle. ECB President Lagarde indicated the pace of future cuts would slow as eurozone inflation is approaching the 2% target and financial conditions have eased significantly. EUR/USD stabilised around 1.03 following the decision, with markets now pricing in two more cuts in 2026. German Bund yields fell to 2.3%.

headline: China Tech Crackdown Eases as Alibaba and Tencent Resume Growth
summary: China's technology sector staged a strong recovery after Beijing signalled the end of its multi-year China tech regulation crackdown. Alibaba reported its fastest revenue growth in six quarters, while Tencent gaming revenues hit a record. Ant Group received regulatory approval to expand its financial services operations, validating the view that Xi Jinping's government is prioritising economic growth over tech sector control. Hang Seng Tech Index rallied 12% in the week.

headline: Natural Gas Prices Spike on Cold Snap and LNG Export Demand
summary: US natural gas prices at Henry Hub jumped 30% in January as an Arctic cold snap drove heating demand to a three-year high and LNG export terminal capacity ran near full utilisation. European natural gas prices also rose sharply as Russia-Ukraine tensions limited pipeline supply to Central Europe. LNG shipments from the US Gulf Coast set a monthly record, underscoring America's role as the world's largest LNG exporter.

headline: Sovereign Wealth Funds Increase Allocations to AI and Infrastructure
summary: Sovereign wealth funds from Norway, Abu Dhabi, and Singapore disclosed significant increases to their private equity and infrastructure fund allocations, with AI infrastructure and data centres the top themes. The Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global, the world's largest sovereign fund, reported record returns driven by technology stocks and is exploring direct co-investment in AI data centre developments alongside BlackRock and Brookfield.

headline: US Bank Earnings Season: Wells Fargo and Citigroup Beat on Net Interest Margin
summary: Wells Fargo and Citigroup reported stronger-than-expected Q4 earnings, with both banks benefiting from elevated net interest margin following higher-for-longer rates. Wells Fargo's loan growth accelerated 6% quarter-on-quarter while Citigroup's transformation plan showed progress with cost reductions ahead of target. Non-performing loans remained contained across both banks. Bank stocks rallied 4% as investors embraced the robust bank earnings season.

headline: Global IPO Market Awakens with $50 Billion Raised in January
summary: The global IPO market recorded its best January since 2021, with $50 billion raised across 180 listings. The PE exits and IPO pipeline that had been building throughout 2025 began to clear, with technology and healthcare companies the most active sectors. Several AI-focused companies secured premium valuations, reigniting private equity interest in public market exits. US exchanges attracted 60% of global IPO proceeds.

headline: Commercial Real Estate Distress Deepens as Office Vacancy Hits 20%
summary: US commercial real estate office vacancy rates reached 20% nationally, with major markets including San Francisco, Chicago, and New York seeing even higher vacancy as remote work becomes entrenched. Several regional banks flagged elevated commercial real estate loan provisions in Q4 earnings. Private credit lenders stepped in to refinance distressed CRE loans as traditional bank lending tightened under Basel IV capital requirements. Data centres and industrial & logistics assets continued to outperform.

headline: Copper Prices Rally on AI Data Centre and Electric Vehicle Demand
summary: Copper prices rose to $10,200 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange, driven by surging demand from AI data centre construction and electric vehicle production. Each data centre requires up to 15 tonnes of copper per megawatt of capacity, while EVs use four times more copper than conventional vehicles. Supply constraints from Chile and Peru added to the bullish outlook, with Dr. Copper seen as a leading indicator of global economic activity.

headline: DeepSeek AI Model Shocks Markets, NVDA Falls 17% in Single Session
summary: Chinese startup DeepSeek released an AI model claiming performance comparable to leading US LLMs at a fraction of the training cost, sending shockwaves through global technology markets. NVIDIA (NVDA) fell 17% in its worst single-day loss since going public, wiping nearly $600 billion in market capitalisation. The development raised questions about US semiconductor export controls effectiveness and whether AI infrastructure spending could slow. The S&P 500 technology sector fell 6%.

headline: Fed Holds Rates Steady in January, Cites Uncertainty Around Tariffs
summary: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate unchanged at 4.25%–4.5% at its January FOMC meeting, with Chair Powell citing elevated inflation uncertainty, a robust labour market, and the potential inflationary impact of tariffs as reasons for caution. The decision was unanimous. Markets had assigned a small probability to a cut, so equities dipped modestly. The next FOMC meeting in March is now seen as the earliest possible date for any resumption of monetary policy easing.

headline: Microsoft and OpenAI Announce $500 Billion Stargate AI Infrastructure Plan
summary: Microsoft, OpenAI, SoftBank, and Oracle jointly announced Stargate, a $500 billion AI infrastructure investment programme targeting new data centres and AI compute facilities across the United States. The initiative is designed to ensure US leadership in artificial intelligence and create 100,000 jobs. The announcement drove shares of data centre REITs, power utilities, and copper producers sharply higher as investors priced in the massive energy and materials demand implied by the buildout.

headline: India's Rupee Hits Record Low as Dollar Strength Pressures EM FX
summary: The Indian rupee fell to a record low of 87.6 per dollar as dollar strength driven by the DXY index reaching 110 put severe pressure on emerging market currencies. The Reserve Bank of India intervened to slow the rupee's decline, selling USD reserves. EM capital flows turned deeply negative in January, with outflows from Asian bond and equity markets accelerating. The Turkish lira, South African rand, and Indonesian rupiah also hit multi-year lows.

headline: Green Bond Market Reaches $1 Trillion Annual Issuance Milestone
summary: Global green bond issuance reached $1 trillion in 2025 for the first time, according to Climate Bonds Initiative data. Sustainability-linked bonds accounted for an additional $300 billion of the overall ESG debt market. European issuers led with 45% of total volumes, driven by the EU taxonomy regulation and SFDR disclosure requirements. Central banks including the ECB and Bank of England also increased their green bond holdings in asset purchase programmes.

headline: US GDP Grows 2.3% in Q4 2025, Full Year at 2.8%, Defying Slowdown Fears
summary: US GDP grew at an annualised rate of 2.3% in Q4 2025, bringing full-year 2025 growth to 2.8%. Consumer spending remained the primary growth driver, rising 3.1% in the quarter. Business investment in equipment and intellectual property was boosted by AI-related capital expenditure. Government spending also contributed positively. The resilient economic performance challenges recession narratives and complicates the case for aggressive Fed monetary policy easing.

headline: BRICS Nations Accelerate De-dollarisation Efforts with New Payment System
summary: BRICS nations including Russia, China, India, Brazil, and newly admitted members launched a cross-border payment infrastructure to reduce dependence on the US dollar in international trade. The BRICS expansion currency initiative aims to settle commodity trades in local currencies, bypassing SWIFT. Analysts estimate de-dollarisation could affect 15–20% of global trade flows over the next decade. The US Treasury dismissed the initiative as economically marginal.

headline: Alphabet Google Reports AI-Driven Search Revenue Acceleration
summary: Alphabet reported Q4 revenue of $96.5 billion, up 12% year-on-year, with Google Search benefiting from AI Overviews driving higher ad click-through rates. Google Cloud revenue rose 30% to $12 billion. CEO Sundar Pichai announced plans to invest $75 billion in AI infrastructure in 2026. The strong results helped offset concerns raised by the DeepSeek AI development and reaffirmed Alphabet's position as a leading artificial intelligence company.

headline: US Imposes 25% Steel and Aluminium Tariffs, Canada and Mexico Retaliate
summary: The US imposed 25% tariffs on steel and aluminium imports from all countries including allies, triggering immediate retaliation from Canada and Mexico. Canada announced counter-tariffs on $30 billion of US goods, while Mexico targeted agricultural products and manufactured goods. The materials and industrials sectors fell on concerns about supply chain disruptions and input cost inflation. US auto manufacturers warned of production cost increases.

headline: Bitcoin Stabilises Above $95,000 as ETF Inflows Resume
summary: Bitcoin stabilised above $95,000 as spot Bitcoin ETF inflows resumed following a three-week drought. BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC led inflows totalling $800 million in the week. On-chain data showed long-term holders accumulating at current prices while short-term speculators reduced exposure. Institutional demand from corporate treasuries, with Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) purchasing an additional 7,633 BTC, provided a price floor.

headline: Amazon AWS Beats Expectations with 28% Revenue Growth on AI Workloads
summary: Amazon Web Services reported Q4 revenue of $28.8 billion, growing 28% year-on-year, beating consensus estimates as enterprise AI and machine learning adoption on cloud computing platforms accelerated. CEO Andy Jassy highlighted AI as the largest growth driver in AWS history. Amazon announced a $100 billion capital expenditure plan for 2026, primarily targeting data centres and AI compute infrastructure. AMZN shares rose 5% in after-hours trading.

headline: Ukraine Peace Negotiations Resume Under US Mediation
summary: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire negotiations resumed in Riyadh under US and Saudi Arabian mediation, raising cautious optimism in European energy and defence markets. Natural gas prices in Europe fell 8% on the prospect of a peace deal restoring some pipeline supply routes. Defence stocks pulled back from recent highs while European reconstruction plays in materials and industrials rallied. A full ceasefire remains uncertain, with territorial disputes unresolved.

headline: US Credit Card Delinquencies Rise to 10-Year High, Consumer Stress Growing
summary: US credit card delinquency rates rose to their highest level since 2013 at 3.2%, according to Federal Reserve data. Non-performing loans in consumer credit portfolios rose at regional banks including Capital One and Synchrony Financial. The rise in delinquencies signals growing consumer financial stress, particularly among lower-income households. Banks increased loan loss provisions in Q4 earnings to reflect deteriorating credit quality in unsecured consumer lending.

headline: OPEC+ Considers Deeper Cuts as Oil Demand Outlook Darkens
summary: OPEC+ convened an emergency meeting after IEA revised down its 2026 oil demand growth forecast to 900,000 barrels per day, citing economic slowdown in China and tariff-driven global trade weakness. Saudi Arabia proposed additional voluntary production cuts of 500,000 barrels per day to support Brent crude prices above $70. The internal debate within OPEC+ centres on balancing short-term price support against long-term market share protection.

headline: Lithium Prices Collapse 70%, Wiping Out EV Battery Sector Margins
summary: Lithium carbonate prices collapsed 70% from their 2022 peak, falling to $10,000 per tonne, as oversupply from Australian and South American mines overwhelmed demand growth from electric vehicle battery production. Several lithium producers announced mine closures and output cuts. The rare earths and lithium-ion battery supply chain faces a prolonged adjustment period. EV manufacturers including Tesla and BYD benefited from lower input costs but battery suppliers faced severe margin compression.

headline: US January CPI Rises 3.0%, Highest in 8 Months, Markets Rattled
summary: US Consumer Price Index rose 3.0% year-on-year in January, the highest reading in eight months and well above the 2.9% consensus estimate. Core CPI jumped 3.3%, driven by shelter, food, and medical services. The hotter-than-expected inflation data sent the 10-year Treasury yield above 4.9% and triggered a sharp equity sell-off, with the S&P 500 falling 2%. Fed funds futures pushed back the first rate cut expectation to September 2026.

headline: Ant Group IPO Cleared by Chinese Regulators After Four-Year Freeze
summary: China's securities regulator approved Ant Group's plan to relist following a four-year freeze stemming from the China tech regulation crackdown. The fintech giant, majority-owned by Alibaba's Jack Ma, was valued at $150 billion in preliminary discussions with underwriters — significantly below its peak $300 billion valuation at the time of its aborted 2020 IPO. The clearance signals Beijing's desire to revive confidence in the private sector.

headline: Private Credit Overtakes High Yield Bonds as Preferred Corporate Finance Tool
summary: Private credit surpassed high yield bonds as the preferred financing tool for leveraged buyouts and corporate refinancings for the first time, according to data from PitchBook and LCD. The $1.7 trillion private credit market attracted $300 billion in new fundraising in 2025. Direct lending funds from Apollo, Ares, and Blackstone dominated deal flow. Basel IV capital requirements are expected to further reduce bank participation in leveraged loans, cementing private credit's dominance.

headline: Eurozone Manufacturing PMI Rises for First Time in Two Years
summary: The Eurozone Manufacturing PMI rose to 47.3 in January, its highest level in two years, though still below the 50 expansion threshold. Germany's PMI improved to 45.4 on early signs of industrial stabilisation, while Spain and Italy recorded sub-50 readings driven by construction and consumer goods sectors. The ECB's rate cuts are beginning to filter through to credit conditions, with loan growth turning positive for the first time since Q2 2024.

headline: Gold Retreats to $2,700 as Dollar Strength Weighs on Precious Metals
summary: Gold prices pulled back to $2,700 per troy ounce as the US dollar index (DXY) climbed to 110, reducing the attractiveness of dollar-denominated bullion for international buyers. The XAU/USD pair found technical support at the 200-day moving average. Central bank demand remained robust, with Poland, Czechia, and Singapore adding to reserves. Analysts maintained medium-term bullish outlook for gold amid geopolitical uncertainty and long-term dollar diversification trends.

headline: Tesla Reports 8% EV Sales Decline as Competition Intensifies
summary: Tesla reported an 8% decline in global electric vehicle deliveries in Q4 2025, its second consecutive quarter of falling sales, as competition from BYD, Volkswagen, and emerging Chinese EV brands intensified. CEO Elon Musk attributed the decline to the model transition period ahead of the refreshed Model Y launch. Consumer discretionary sector analysts noted that Tesla's brand perception has been affected by Musk's political activities, with US consumer sentiment surveys showing increased buyer hesitancy.

headline: Federal Reserve Meeting Minutes Reveal Deep Division on Rate Path
summary: Minutes from the January FOMC meeting revealed significant disagreement among Federal Reserve officials about the appropriate pace of monetary policy easing, with several members arguing for an extended pause and others concerned about labour market weakening. The minutes highlighted uncertainty around the inflationary impact of tariffs, fiscal stimulus, and immigration policy changes. Market participants interpreted the divisions as a signal that the Fed will remain on hold for longer than previously expected.

headline: Carbon Market Prices Drop 25% as EU ETS Reform Faces Political Headwinds
summary: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) carbon prices fell 25% to €48 per tonne amid political uncertainty over proposed ETS reform and growing opposition from energy-intensive industries facing competitiveness pressures. The carbon market decline reduces the economic incentive for companies to invest in clean energy transition assets. Green bond spreads widened slightly on the news, and several sustainability-linked bonds with carbon-related KPIs were repriced lower.

headline: India GDP Beats Forecasts at 7.6% for Q3, Becomes Fifth Largest Economy
summary: India's GDP grew 7.6% year-on-year in Q3 FY2026, significantly ahead of IMF estimates, propelling the country past the UK to become the world's fifth largest economy by nominal GDP. Infrastructure spending and digital services exports drove the outperformance. The Reserve Bank of India held rates steady, balancing growth support with rupee stability concerns. India growth is expected to average 6.8% in FY2027, with demographic tailwinds and manufacturing nearshoring providing structural support.

headline: Semiconductor Supply Chain Diversification Accelerates with New Arizona and Germany Fabs
summary: Intel and TSMC announced major milestones in semiconductor supply chain diversification, with Intel's Arizona fab entering high-volume production of 3nm chips and TSMC's Dresden, Germany facility breaking ground. The chip supply diversification effort, backed by the US CHIPS Act and EU Chips Act, aims to reduce dependence on Taiwan for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. ASML delivered a record 10 EUV lithography machines in Q4, supporting the global capacity build-out.

headline: Hedge Fund Short Sellers Target US Regional Banks Over CRE Exposure
summary: Major hedge funds disclosed large short positions against US regional banks with elevated commercial real estate loan concentrations. Office vacancy rates exceeding 20% in major cities have raised concerns about loan-to-value ratios on maturing CRE loans. Non-performing loan ratios at some smaller banks rose above 3%, triggering regulatory scrutiny. Shadow banking and private credit lenders are positioning to refinance or take over distressed CRE assets as traditional bank lending tightens.

headline: Ethereum Staking Yields Rise to 4.8% Following Network Upgrade
summary: Ethereum's Pectra network upgrade successfully launched, improving staking efficiency and raising annualised staking yields to 4.8%. Over 34% of all circulating Ethereum supply is now staked, creating significant supply constraints. The upgrade also expanded Layer 2 scaling capacity, reducing transaction costs to under $0.01. Institutional adoption of Ethereum through spot ETFs accelerated post-upgrade, with custody solutions from Fidelity and Coinbase attracting asset manager interest.

headline: Germany Fiscal Stimulus Package Boosts European Defence and Infrastructure Stocks
summary: Germany's new coalition government announced a landmark fiscal stimulus package worth €500 billion over 10 years, suspending the constitutional debt brake to fund infrastructure spending and defence rearmament. The package triggered a significant bond market repricing, with German Bund yields rising 40 basis points — the largest single-day move since reunification. Defence & aerospace stocks surged across Europe, with Rheinmetall, BAE Systems, and Leonardo rallying 12–18% on the news.

headline: S&P 500 Enters Correction Territory, Falls 10% from Peak
summary: The S&P 500 entered official correction territory, falling more than 10% from its February all-time high, driven by tariff uncertainty, rising Treasury yields, and slowing corporate earnings growth expectations. Tech stocks and consumer discretionary led declines, with the Nasdaq falling 14% from its peak. The VIX fear gauge spiked to 28, its highest level since August 2024. Portfolio managers increased cash allocations and rotated into defensive sectors including utilities and consumer staples.

headline: China's People's Bank Cuts Reserve Requirements for Third Time This Cycle
summary: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) cut the reserve requirement ratio by 50 basis points, releasing approximately $140 billion in liquidity into the banking system — the third cut in the current easing cycle. The PBOC also lowered the 1-year loan prime rate by 10bps to 3.0%. China's stimulus efforts aim to offset the drag from US tariffs on Chinese exports, which have accelerated since January. The yuan remained stable near 7.3 per dollar as PBOC managed capital outflow pressures.

headline: US February CPI Moderates Slightly to 2.8%, But Remains Elevated
summary: US CPI rose 2.8% year-on-year in February, a slight moderation from January's 3.0% but still above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. Core inflation of 3.1% reflected persistent services price pressures, particularly in housing and insurance. Tariff-related goods price increases are only beginning to feed through to the CPI basket, raising concerns that inflation could re-accelerate in Q2. Markets trimmed rate cut expectations further, with only one cut now fully priced for 2026.

headline: AI Power Demand Threatens US Grid Stability, Utilities Issue Warning
summary: Major US electric utilities including Duke Energy and NextEra warned that AI data centre power demand could strain grid infrastructure as soon as 2027 if transmission capacity is not upgraded urgently. AI data centre construction driven by the Stargate initiative and hyperscaler capital expenditure is expected to add 47 gigawatts of electricity demand by 2030. Nuclear power is increasingly viewed as the only scalable clean energy source capable of meeting baseload requirements, with Microsoft and Amazon signing reactor power purchase agreements.

headline: European Defence Stocks at Record Highs as NATO Spending Commitments Rise
summary: European defence & aerospace stocks reached record highs as NATO members accelerated pledges to increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP following Germany's historic fiscal package. Rheinmetall's order backlog hit €50 billion, while Leonardo and Thales reported record quarterly revenue from ammunition and military electronics. The defence sector has become the top-performing segment of European equity markets, outperforming technology and financials year-to-date.

headline: Bitcoin Drops Below $80,000 as Macro Uncertainty and Tariff Fear Drive Risk-Off
summary: Bitcoin fell below $80,000 for the first time since November, caught in the broader risk-off sell-off driven by US tariff escalation, equity market corrections, and rising Treasury yields. The correlation between Bitcoin and equities rose above 0.7, frustrating proponents of crypto as a portfolio diversifier. On-chain data showed long-term holders reducing exposure for the first time in three months. Strategy disclosed an unrealised loss on its Bitcoin holdings for the first time.

headline: US Antitrust Regulators Challenge Google's Search Advertising Monopoly
summary: The US Department of Justice filed new remedies in its landmark antitrust case against Alphabet's Google, seeking structural remedies including mandatory divestiture of the Chrome browser and potentially the Android operating system. The antitrust & big tech case represents the most significant challenge to a technology company's market position since the Microsoft antitrust case of the 1990s. GOOG shares fell 6% on the news. The case is expected to take two to three years to reach a final resolution.

headline: Fed's Powell Reaffirms Data Dependency, Signals No Rush to Cut Rates
summary: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell testified before the Senate Banking Committee, reaffirming that the Fed is in no rush to cut rates given lingering inflation risks and a resilient labour market. Powell acknowledged uncertainty from tariff policy but said it was too early to determine the net effect on inflation and growth. The testimony reinforced the view that monetary policy will remain restrictive through at least mid-2026. Treasury yields rose modestly on his comments.

headline: Brent Crude Falls Below $68 on Demand Slowdown Fears and Dollar Strength
summary: Brent crude oil fell below $68 per barrel, its lowest level since July 2024, as a combination of demand slowdown fears driven by global trade tensions and continued dollar strength weighed on prices. The IEA cut its 2026 demand growth forecast to 700,000 barrels per day, while US crude oil production continued to set records at 13.6 million bpd. OPEC+ held an emergency call but members were unable to agree on deeper cuts in the short term.

headline: Gold Surges to New All-Time High of $2,950 as Safe Haven Flows Return
summary: Gold hit a new all-time high of $2,950 per troy ounce as investors fled to safe haven assets amid escalating US-China trade tensions, S&P 500 correction concerns, and uncertainty over Federal Reserve monetary policy. The XAU/USD pair's breakout above $2,800 attracted significant momentum buying. Central bank gold purchases from China and emerging market economies remain at record levels. Silver also rallied, with the gold-to-silver ratio compressing to 88.

headline: Nvidia Blackwell GPU Production Ramps, Data Centre Backlog at Record
summary: Nvidia reported that its next-generation Blackwell GPU architecture is ramping faster than any product in the company's history, with hyperscalers placing multi-year supply agreements worth hundreds of billions of dollars. The data centre backlog reached $45 billion, providing revenue visibility through 2027. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted that AI inference demand — running trained models at scale — is emerging as a new growth driver alongside AI training workloads, expanding the total addressable market for semiconductor chips.

headline: US Consumer Confidence Falls to Lowest Since 2022, Recession Fears Rise
summary: The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index fell to 92.9 in February, its lowest reading since 2022 and the third consecutive monthly decline. Consumers cited concerns about job security, rising prices from tariffs, and stock market volatility as the primary negative factors. The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment survey showed a similar deterioration, with inflation expectations rising to 4.3% for the year ahead. Consumer spending in consumer discretionary categories showed early signs of softening.

headline: Mexico Nearshoring Boom Accelerates as US Tariffs Drive Supply Chain Shifts
summary: Mexico emerged as one of the primary beneficiaries of US tariff policy, with foreign direct investment in manufacturing nearshoring facilities reaching $45 billion in 2025, a 60% increase year-on-year. Automotive, electronics, and consumer goods manufacturers accelerated factory relocations from China to northern Mexico. The Mexican peso initially strengthened on FDI inflows before falling when broader tariff threats targeting Mexico were announced. Mexico nearshoring is reshaping North American supply chains.

headline: Corporate Bankruptcy Filings Rise 20% Year-on-Year in Early 2026
summary: US corporate bankruptcy and restructuring filings rose 20% year-on-year in January and February 2026 as companies that loaded up on cheap debt during the 2020–2022 era face refinancing walls at much higher interest rates. Retail and commercial real estate were the hardest hit sectors. Distressed debt funds raised a combined $80 billion in Q4 2025 and early 2026 in anticipation of increased deal flow. Chapter 11 filings by mid-sized companies are at the highest level since the 2009 financial crisis.

headline: Bank of England Cuts Rates to 4.25%, Signals Further Easing in 2026
summary: The Bank of England cut its base rate by 25 basis points to 4.25% at its March meeting, with the Monetary Policy Committee voting 7-2 in favour of the cut. Governor Andrew Bailey cited slowing inflation and weakening UK economic growth as justification. GBP/USD fell 0.5% on the decision but found support near 1.29. The BoE projected two further cuts in 2026 if inflation continues to moderate toward the 2% target. UK house prices rose modestly following the rate decision.

headline: AI Regulation Framework Proposed by EU, Could Restrict High-Risk Applications
summary: The European Union's AI Act entered its operational phase, requiring companies deploying high-risk artificial intelligence systems in biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, and employment to comply with new transparency and human oversight rules. The regulation affects major US technology companies including Microsoft, Google, and Meta that operate AI services in European markets. Non-compliance fines can reach 7% of global annual revenue. Several AI startups are restructuring their EU operations in response.

headline: TSMC Reports February Revenue Up 39%, Demand Outstrips Production Capacity
summary: TSMC reported February revenue of NT$260 billion, up 39% year-on-year, as demand for advanced semiconductor chips from AI chip designers including NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, and Broadcom far exceeded available production capacity. The Taiwanese chipmaker's 3nm and 5nm nodes are fully booked through 2026, with customers pre-ordering capacity for 2027. TSMC announced plans to raise chip prices 5–10% in 2026 reflecting pricing power in the semiconductor supply chain.

headline: US Unemployment Rate Rises to 4.3% in February as Hiring Slows
summary: US unemployment rose to 4.3% in February as non-farm payrolls added only 151,000 jobs, below the 160,000 consensus estimate. Government employment fell as federal workforce reductions began taking effect. The labour market is showing early signs of softening, with temporary employment declining and the average workweek shortening to 34.1 hours. Fed officials noted the data does not yet warrant a policy change but bears monitoring, keeping rate cut expectations anchored to Q3 2026.

headline: Private Equity LBO Activity Rebounds as Financing Conditions Ease
summary: Leveraged buyout activity rebounded in Q1 2026 with $180 billion in announced deals, up 45% from Q1 2025, as private credit and loan markets eased funding conditions. Blackstone's $14 billion buyout of a logistics real estate platform was the largest LBO in two years. PE funds are targeting industrials, healthcare, and technology companies where AI integration creates operational value creation opportunities. The PE exits and IPO pipeline backlog remains large but markets are gradually absorbing new listings.

headline: China Rare Earth Export Restrictions Target US Defence Supply Chain
summary: China announced export restrictions on seven rare earth elements critical for US defence and technology manufacturing, including neodymium, dysprosium, and terbium used in fighter jet engines, missile guidance systems, and EV motors. The move is seen as retaliation for US semiconductor export controls. Critical minerals supply chain security has become a top priority for the US, UK, EU, and Australia, with new mining subsidies and strategic stockpiling programmes announced.

headline: Tech Stocks Recover as Tariff Pause Hopes Spark Risk Rally
summary: Technology stocks staged a sharp recovery after reports emerged that the Trump administration was considering a 90-day tariff pause for key trading partners engaged in good-faith negotiations. The Nasdaq rose 3.5% in its best single day since November, with AI and machine learning stocks leading gains. NVDA surged 8%, recovering a portion of losses from the DeepSeek-driven sell-off. The S&P 500 rallied 2.1%, reducing the depth of the correction to 7% from its February peak.

headline: ECB Balance Sheet Shrinks Below €6 Trillion as Quantitative Tightening Accelerates
summary: The European Central Bank's balance sheet fell below €6 trillion for the first time since 2020 as quantitative tightening through non-reinvestment of maturing PEPP and APP bonds accelerated. The reduction in central bank liquidity is tightening financial conditions in peripheral eurozone bond markets, with Italian BTP spreads over German Bunds widening to 130 basis points. The ECB confirmed it will review its QT pace at the June policy meeting in light of euro area growth concerns.

headline: Stablecoin Market Cap Reaches $250 Billion as Regulatory Clarity Improves
summary: The total stablecoin market capitalisation reached $250 billion following the US Senate's passage of the GENIUS Act, which established a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins for the first time. Tether (USDT) and Circle's USDC account for 80% of the market. Major banks including JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citi are exploring proprietary stablecoin issuance under the new crypto regulation regime. The development is seen as a transformative moment for digital asset infrastructure.

headline: Iron Ore Falls to $95 on Chinese Steel Demand Weakness
summary: Iron ore prices fell to $95 per tonne, the lowest since 2022, as Chinese steel production declined amid the ongoing China property sector slump and government-mandated output restrictions to meet carbon reduction targets. Australian and Brazilian miners including BHP, Rio Tinto, and Vale saw shares fall 5–8%. Copper and aluminium also weakened on growth concerns, with the broader commodity supercycle narrative facing renewed scrutiny. China's infrastructure stimulus is the key swing factor for metal demand in 2026.

headline: US Healthcare Sector M&A Heats Up as AI Diagnostics Drive Consolidation
summary: US healthcare M&A activity surged in Q1 2026, with $120 billion in announced deals as large pharmaceutical and hospital groups acquired AI diagnostics and digital health startups. UnitedHealth acquired an AI-powered radiology platform for $8.2 billion while CVS Health purchased a pharmacy benefit management AI company. The FDA's accelerated approval pathway for AI medical devices is driving valuations and deal activity in the pharmaceuticals & biotech and healthcare technology sub-sectors.

headline: GBP/USD Tests 1.30 Resistance as UK Economic Data Surprises to Upside
summary: Sterling tested the 1.30 level against the dollar after UK services PMI surprised to the upside at 53.2 and retail sales rose 0.4% month-on-month. The GBP/USD pair has outperformed most G10 currency pairs year-to-date, supported by resilient UK economic data and a relatively hawkish Bank of England compared to ECB peers. However, ongoing trade policy uncertainty regarding UK-US relations and EU-UK post-Brexit trade talks caps the cable's upside potential.

headline: Blackstone Infrastructure Fund Closes at $30 Billion, Eyes Data Centres and Energy Grids
summary: Blackstone's latest infrastructure fund closed at $30 billion, the largest infrastructure fund ever raised, with sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, and insurance companies as the primary investors. The fund's investment focus centres on AI data centres, power grid upgrades, LNG export terminals, and renewables assets. Blackstone cited the $300 billion annual infrastructure funding gap in the United States as the primary investment opportunity, with real assets providing inflation protection and stable cash yields for institutional allocators.
